questions.stem: In which domain is the term Entropy normally used when applied to data?
options: Network Security
Data Science
Data Warehousing
Database Administration
Project Management
questions.explanation: Entropy is normally used in the Data Science domain, where finding unexpected outcomes is the aim.

questions.stem: What does High Entropy mean in a dataset?
options: The data has been fully validated
All values are identical
The data is ready for reporting
More surprises and more unexpected values, which are considered more informative
Fewer surprises and less informative values
questions.explanation: High Entropy means more surprises; more unexpected values are considered more informative.

questions.stem: What does Low Entropy mean in a dataset?
options: Fewer surprises and fewer unexpected values, which are considered less informative
More unexpected values that are highly informative
The data contains many errors
The data cannot be stored
Every value has a probability of zero
questions.explanation: Low Entropy means fewer surprises; less unexpected values are considered less informative.

questions.stem: By what other name is Entropy described?
options: Perfect Order of values
Average Deviation of values
Central Tendency of values
Normal Distribution of values
Extreme Disorder of values
questions.explanation: Entropy is also called the Extreme Disorder of values.

questions.stem: In the plus-and-minus illustration of Entropy from I Am Datapedia!, where is Entropy at its lowest?
options: In the circles where the mix of pluses and minuses cannot be determined
In every circle equally
At the starting point where all the signs are MINUS
Only in the second circle
Wherever the values are hidden
questions.explanation: At the starting point (all MINUS), the 50/50 middle and the end (all PLUS), Entropy is at its lowest because no surprises are expected.

questions.stem: How is probability treated when analysing results in terms of Entropy?
options: The higher the probability, the more informative the outcome
The lower the probability, the better the outcome
Probability is ignored entirely
Only probabilities above 50% are considered
Probability is only used for structured data
questions.explanation: Results are analysed on a probability ratio where the lower the probability, the better, because unexpected outcomes are what is sought.

questions.stem: In the context of Entropy, what counts as informative information?
options: Information that has been verified by an auditor
Information that is repeated in every record
Information that comes from a trusted source
Information stored in a data dictionary
Something that was not already known
questions.explanation: Informative information is something which was not known; surprises are welcomed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT true of how Entropy is used in Data Science?
options: Surprises are avoided at all costs
Finding unexpected outcomes is the aim
Results are analysed based on a probability ratio
It helps Data Scientists try to predict unknown values
More unexpected values are considered more informative
questions.explanation: In Entropy analysis surprises are welcomed, not avoided, because unexpected outcomes are the most informative.

questions.stem: What is the situation for a Data Scientist when Entropy in a dataset is at its lowest?
options: The data must be discarded
The model will produce the most surprises
The data is at its most informative
No surprises are expected, so there is not much to predict
The probability of every value is unknown
questions.explanation: Where Entropy is lowest, no surprises are expected, so there is nothing much for Data Scientists to predict.

questions.stem: What do Data Scientists use the concept of Entropy for?
options: Compressing datasets before storage
Designing database schemas
Finding unknown values and trying to predict them
Assigning user access rights
Scheduling batch jobs
questions.explanation: Entropy is how Data Scientists find unknown values and try to predict them, focusing on the points where the outcome is hardest to determine.
